Rate limits: set_quota(key, tokens) caps a key's total tokens and returns the quota; it throws if the key has already used more. record_usage must throw if the call would take the key over its quota. Keys without a quota are unlimited.
(defn over_quota? [key extra] (let [q (quota_for_key key)] (and (some? q) (> (+ (used_tokens_for_key key) extra) q))))

(defn set_quota [key tokens] (when-not (and (string? key) (not (blank? key))) (throw (ex-info "key must be a non-empty string" {}))) (when-not (and (number? tokens) (not (< tokens 0))) (throw (ex-info "quota must be a non-negative number" {}))) (when (> (used_tokens_for_key key) tokens) (throw (ex-info "quota below tokens already used" {}))) (swap-state! assoc-in ["quotas" key] tokens) tokens)

(defn record_usage [key model tokens] (when-not (and (string? key) (not (blank? key))) (throw (ex-info "key must be a non-empty string" {}))) (when-not (and (number? tokens) (not (< tokens 0))) (throw (ex-info "tokens must be a non-negative number" {}))) (when (over_quota? key tokens) (throw (ex-info "call exceeds quota for key" {}))) (swap-state! update "calls" (fnil conj []) (usage_record key model tokens)) (usage_total_for_key key))

Who spends the most? top_spender() returns the key with the highest cost; ties go to the alphabetically first key; null when nothing is recorded.
